item.title: v1.100.0-dev.1
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * fix(responses): keep the conversation when chaining previous_response_id on the bridge by @mateo-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37956 * feat(newrelic): per-team New Relic trace routing via team callbacks by @yucheng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37603 * perf(ci): cache uv dependencies in the lint job by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37783 * perf(ci): fan the budget checkers out across cores by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37784 * ci: port the Postgres suites off CircleCI onto service containers by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37785 * feat(ci): gate patching of SDK internals in tests as TQ008 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37787 * ci: measure enterprise/ coverage by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37788 * ci: run the keyless caching tests that ran in no job by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/37790 * fix(ci): run the migration DDL item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.title: v1.97.0-rc.1
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * fix(azure_sentinel): respect AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST and derive the Azure Monitor audience per item.title: v1.94.2
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.title: v1.96.0-dev.1
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * feat(prometheus): add service_tier label to latency and spend metrics by @yassin-berriai in Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.title: v1.94.0-rc.3
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * chore(release): backport #33810, #33733 to rc/1.94.0 and bump litellm-proxy-extras to 0.4.79.post1 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/34215 * chore(ui): rebuild Next.js bundle on rc/1.94.0 so the Cost Optimization page ships by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/34216 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.94.0-rc.2...v1.94.0-rc.3

This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * chore(release): backport #32542 to stable/1.90.x and cut 1.90.4 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/32937 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.90.3...v1.90.4

item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.title: v1.92.0-rc.1
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * feat(mcp): add all-proxy-mcpservers sentinel to grant teams every MCP server by item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.title: v1.89.3
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * chore(release): backport #30480, #30543, #30542, #30573 to stable/1.89.x and cut 1.89.3 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/30888 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.89.2...v1.89.3

Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * chore(release): backport 1.84.8 patches + #30220 deps to stable/1.86.x and cut 1.86.6 by @yuneng-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/30403 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/compare/v1.86.5...v1.86.6

Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. item.title: v1.89.0-rc.1
item.description: ## Verify Docker Image Signature All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53. **Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):** A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key: **Verify using the release tag (convenience):** Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules: Expected output: --- ## What's Changed * test(responses): bump deprecated gemini-3-pro-preview to gemini-3.1-pro-preview by @mateo-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29433 * fix: map mistral/ministral-8b-latest in model price map by @mateo-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29453 * fix(datadog): split oversized batches on 413 instead of re-queueing forever by @yassin-berriai in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29444 * feat(otel): allowlist team_metadata sub-keys promoted to baggage by @yassin-berriai in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29442 * fix: stop use_chat_completions_api flag from leaking into provider request body by @mateo-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29447 * fix(anthropic, fireworks): inline legacy $ref defs in tool schemas by @milan-berri in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/28646 * fix(proxy): omit
